about: One rail_access topic, rail-cities, that watches the Rail Access Monitor's four starting cities (docs/enhancements/archive/rail-access-monitor.md §2) and writes about one of them a day (docs/enhancements/archive/dailysubject_hook.md §4). It is a complete body for the admin API's POST /topics; docs/deployment-runsheet.md, 'rail_access topics', shows how to create it with scripts/admin_cli.py. Each city's box sits inside one 100 km UTM square, so inside one Sentinel-2 tile. adapter_config sets the four sites, their reach, the 80 s time_budget_seconds cap (Sydney's first OpenStreetMap network takes most of a minute: docs/deployment-runsheet.md, 'rail_access topics') and the rota: Sydney on Monday and Friday, Melbourne on Tuesday and Saturday, Singapore on Wednesday and Sunday, Boston on Thursday, each day as Sydney's calendar has it (rotation_timezone). Every other key takes the rail_access adapter's default (docs/enhancements/archive/vision.md §5); the worker's stop reach (400 m) and feeder reach (2 km) behind the bus, tram and ferry stop measures are params it may override. The research tick measures the cities in turn, one per tick, whatever the day. The daily cycle runs every day at 09:05 Sydney time and writes about the day's city alone, from every Finding about that city since its last article on that city. findings_window_hours is 192 (8 days): Boston's 7 days between its Thursdays, the longest gap in the rota, plus a day for a clock change or a late run (the two-day cities need only 120). The window never reaches back past the city's own last article, so no Finding is drafted twice; one that reports two cities is drafted on each one's day. A day with no new Finding about its city stops before any model call. The editorial goal names no city: the day's mandate adds it. editorial_goals is the standing goal and editorial_goal_rotation the four angles taken in turn on a city's Findings (access, network, simulations, transit: docs/RailVisionSeeding.md §3 and §7). All five say the same things in plain words: reach is straight-line distance to the nearest mapped station or bus, tram or ferry stop, and minutes are that distance at 80 m a minute, never a journey time; every simulated link is theoretical, a what-if on the mapped graph justified by its numbers and qualified by what its straight line crosses, never a route or a recommendation; the register is constructive, with no complaint, cost, political or resource-allocation view; the efficiency of the mapped stops (built-up km² within reach per 100 stops, the overlap with station reach) and the multimodal isolation weight are named as what they measure; nothing is said that is not in the findings. Adding a city means adding a site and giving it a day in the rota; every site needs one. force_manual_review is forced on for this adapter whether or not it is sent.

editorial_goals.primary_focus: Rail and transit access in the day's city, analysed from the findings alone. Title it plainly after what was measured; open with what the measures are: built-up density from Sentinel-2 imagery and straight-line reach over OpenStreetMap's stations and bus, tram and ferry stops; minutes are that distance at 80 m a minute, never a journey time. Then the numbers: the share of built-up area within reach of a station and, where given, of any stop, the area beyond, station and stop counts, the scene's date and coverage, and any change from earlier scenes. Then each rule-based flag the findings carry (single point of failure, isolated high demand, ghost line): the station, what it measures, its multimodal isolation weight where given. Then each simulated link, always theoretical: a what-if on the mapped graph and straight lines, justified by its numbers and what its line crosses, never a route or recommendation. Say what the measures show and what a link would change; point to each map once.
editorial_goals.exclusion_criteria: No ridership, patronage, frequency, journey, travel or waiting time, cost, funding, population, income or other demographic claim: built-up density measures structures, not people, and minutes are walking time over a straight line. No recommendation to build, extend or close anything, no route or alignment, no forecast and no cause. No complaint, blame or criticism of transport agencies, governments, politicians or zoning, and no cost, funding, political or resource-allocation view: say what the measures show and what a theoretical link would change, never what anyone should have done. No absolute judgement that a place is badly served or unlivable. No comparison with a city the findings do not measure. Nothing from outside the findings (strikes, fares, rolling stock, timetables, plans). Name a flag, link or station only if the findings carry it; no number or place name that is not in the findings.

editorial_goal_rotation.name: access
editorial_goal_rotation.primary_focus: Rail and transit access in the day's city through walking reach, from the findings alone. Title it plainly after what was measured. Open by saying what the measures are: built-up density from Sentinel-2 imagery and straight-line reach over OpenStreetMap's rail stations and mapped bus, tram and ferry stops, with minutes as that distance at 80 m a minute, never a journey time. Lead with the share of built-up area within reach of a station and the built-up area beyond it; where the findings give it, put the share within reach of any mapped stop or station beside the rail-only one, with the area beyond all of them. Then the station count, the scene's capture date and coverage, and any change against the city's earlier scenes. Point to the rail map once, saying what its warm colours and outlined areas show. Say what the measures show, never a complaint or a cost, political or resource-allocation view. Give the flags and simulations one sentence at most: they have their own articles.

editorial_goal_rotation.name: network
editorial_goal_rotation.primary_focus: The structure of the day's city's mapped rail network, from the findings alone. Title it plainly after the flag it leads with. Open by saying the flags are rule-based readings of OpenStreetMap's topology and built-up density, not ridership or service. Take each rule-based flag the findings carry in turn (single point of failure, isolated high demand, ghost line): the station or stations it names, what the flag measures (shortest paths through the network, distance to a hub, activity along a chain), and the figure behind it. Where the findings give a station's multimodal isolation weight, put it beside the rail one and say what it is: the rail weight discounted by the share of the station's hinterland that mapped bus, tram and ferry stops reach. Give the served share and station count once, as context. Say what the measures show, never a complaint, blame or criticism of anyone. Point to the rail map once: flagged stations are ringed in red. Name only stations the findings name.

editorial_goal_rotation.name: simulations
editorial_goal_rotation.primary_focus: The theoretical links for the day's city's mapped rail network, from the findings alone. Title it plainly after the link it leads with. Open by saying every link is theoretical: a rule-based what-if on OpenStreetMap's topology and straight-line distances, not a route, an alignment, a plan, a cost or a recommendation. Take each link the findings carry (orbital link, feeder corridor): the stations it joins, its length, its justification in the numbers (the stations' isolation weights and distances to a hub, the fall in hub distance, how many stations it brings closer) and what its straight line crosses (water, ground the scene could not see), always in conditional words ('in the model', 'the simulation suggests'). Say what each link would change, never a cost, political or resource-allocation view. Give the served share and any flag the link answers once, as context. Point to the rail map once: theoretical links are dashed. Name only stations the findings name.

editorial_goal_rotation.name: transit
editorial_goal_rotation.primary_focus: Transit reach across modes in the day's city, from the findings alone. Title it plainly after what was measured. Open by saying the measures are straight-line reach to the nearest mapped bus, tram or ferry stop and rail station over OpenStreetMap, with minutes as that distance at 80 m a minute, never a journey time. Lead with the share of built-up area within walking reach of any mapped stop or station against the rail-only share, and the area beyond all of them. Then how efficiently the mapped stops cover built-up ground: the km² within reach per 100 stops and the overlap with station reach; how many of the largest rail deserts the stops mostly cover (half or more of a patch within stop reach); the stop counts by mode; the scene's date and coverage. Point to the transit-reach map once, saying what its three fills show. Constructive: what the measures show, never a complaint or a cost, political or resource-allocation view. No number or place name that is not in the findings.
